definition: In the theory of matching markets, an optimal stable matching is a matching that, among all stable matchings, satisfies some criterion of optimality.
details: In the special case in which the matching market is bipartite (e.g. there are men and women, each man should be matched to woman and each woman should be matched to a man), the problem is called optimal stable marriage. This is a challenging optimization problem, as even in the bipartite case, the number of stable marriages might be exponential in the number of agents.

explainer.lead: It is a matching among all stable matchings that satisfies some criterion of optimality. It matters because stable matchings can be numerous, making the optimal one hard to find.

tiers.eli5: Many pairings keep everyone from wanting to swap, and this picks the best of those acceptable pairings.
tiers.practitioner: In bipartite markets, designers search over stable matchings for the one meeting their objective; the number of stable matchings can be exponential in the number of agents, making exhaustive search impractical.
tiers.paperLevel: Among all stable matchings of a matching market, select one satisfying an optimality criterion; in the bipartite case (optimal stable marriage) the number of stable marriages can be exponential in the number of agents.

explainer.example: In a market of men and women, all stable marriages are considered and the one optimising the chosen criterion is selected.
